category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: Landlord refusing repairs causing damage
expected: Explains landlord's structural maintenance obligations and tenant's right to issue notice or deduct urgent repairs.
prompt: The roof has severe water leakage damaging my furniture. Landlord refuses to fix it despite multiple requests. What are my rights?
raw_response:
Hello! I am LawPilot AI, your expert and ethical Indian legal assistant, and I am here to help you navigate this difficult situation with your landlord.

### | Your Situation
You are facing severe roof water leakage in your rented premises that is damaging your personal furniture, and your landlord is refusing to carry out the necessary repairs despite multiple requests. This failure by the landlord violates basic tenancy maintenance obligations and threatens your peaceful enjoyment of the property.

### | Your Legal Position
* Under Indian tenancy principles, including the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and Model Tenancy Act guidelines, a landlord is obligated to keep the structural premises in a habitable and tenantable condition unless agreed otherwise in writing.
* Water leakage originating from the roof constitutes a structural defect which is strictly the landlord's responsibility to repair, not yours.
* Reasonable wear and tear refers to the natural deterioration of a property over time through normal usage, whereas severe roof leakage and resulting furniture damage go far beyond normal wear and tear, engaging the landlord's liability for breach of statutory maintenance duties.
* Under essential services and quiet enjoyment provisions (such as principles under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999, Section 29), withholding necessary structural upkeep that renders the premises uninhabitable can be treated as a breach of statutory duties.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Take clear photographs and videos of the active water leakage, damaged furniture, and save all written text messages, emails, or call logs showing your previous requests to the landlord.
2. Send a written demand notice: Issue a formal written legal notice to your landlord detailing the damage, demanding immediate roof repairs and compensation or rent adjustment for furniture damage, and granting a clear timeframe of 15 days to comply.
3. Appropriate forum: If the landlord fails to act within 15 days, you may approach the local Rent Authority or Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission for deficiency in housing services, or file a civil suit for mandatory injunction and damages.

### Information I still need from you
1. In which city and state is this rented property located, and do you have a registered or written rent agreement?
2. Approximately how much financial loss have you suffered due to the furniture damage caused by the leakage?

citations.title: Relief against forfeiture and prohibition against cutting off essential supplies
citations.description: No landlord shall without just or sufficient cause cut off or withhold any essential supply or service (water, electricity, lifts) enjoyed by the tenant. Violation is punishable with imprisonment or fine.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
